request.prompt: View 1, Kelderby seen from the sea, from a boat some eighty blocks south of the quay, at eye height just above the water, in late afternoon light. The whole town fills the frame. In front, the harbour basin and the quay: a long straight stone wharf about two blocks out of the water with square bollards, stacked crates and nets, small fishing boats moored along it, and the harbourmaster's stone house at its right-hand (east) end. From the middle of the quay one broad main street climbs straight up the slope away from the viewer, northward, in ten short flights of shallow steps between level cobbled stretches, the houses along both sides stepping up the hill so their roofs rise like stairs; a few narrow side lanes leave it to left and right, and festival bunting crosses the street. At the top of the street is a cobbled square: on its right (east) side the tall west front of a large Gothic cathedral with flying buttresses and a tall bell tower at its north-west corner, its long nave running away to the east; on its left (west) side a large timber-framed coaching inn. Behind and above the square rises a steep green mountain, and on its summit, about eighty blocks higher than the square, stands a square grey Scottish tower-house castle with a tall gatehouse tower, a long hall range and a curtain wall, reached by a long cobbled road that zig-zags up the mountain's flank from the square. On the right of the frame a rocky green headland runs out into the sea on the east side of the harbour, a narrow cliff path along its spine, and at its far seaward tip a tall white lighthouse with a small keeper's cottage in a walled yard. Open blue sea on the left.
request.style_note: Kelderby, a cheerful stone-and-timber harbour town on the slope below a castle mountain, on the afternoon of its yearly Founders' Play, drawn in the same hand throughout: warm painterly storybook concept painting, bright and friendly, clear sky, golden late-afternoon sun from the west, honey light on grey stone-brick walls and dark spruce and oak timber, dark slate-blue tile roofs, a deep blue sea, green turf and flower boxes of red poppies, blue cornflowers and white daisies, strings of bright festival bunting and painted banners strung across the streets for the play. Everything is massed from large squared blocks with flat faces and clean right angles so every form could be built block by block in Minecraft: the houses are rectangular stone boxes with timber upper storeys and steep gable roofs, the main street is a broad cobbled street stepping down the slope in short flights of shallow steps, the quay is a straight stone wall with square bollards. People, where any appear, are ordinary townsfolk in plain wool, linen and aprons, never armoured, never armed. Nothing glows but lanterns and windows. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, text or border.
